repairs.after: {"q": "Which kinds of workloads does the proposal say bear the real cost of today's recreate-to-resize behaviour, and which kind mostly tolerates it?", "answer": "Low-replica services, stateful workloads and batch jobs pay in lower availability or higher cost; stateless workloads are generally designed to withstand the disruption", "accept": ["stateless, versus stateful, batch and low replica", "stateful, batch and low replica workloads pay in availability or cost, while stateless ones survive recreation", "low replica count services, stateful workloads and batch jobs suffer; stateless workloads mostly tolerate recreation"]}
repairs.rationale: The first repair targeted the right fact (who_is_hurt is verbatim in the brief prompt and in the human span at kep-1287 lines 172-176) but built a 16-content-word lexical key against a 0.8 substring-word bar, so the verify pass measured two clean correct answers at 8/11 = 0.727 and the item became ungradeable. The fix keeps the target and replaces the key with a four-token conjunction: accept[0] normalises to the word list ['stateless','stateful','batch','replica'] and needs 4/4, so every category has to be named and no single omission passes. Stems are chosen to survive inflection under the matcher's substring word test: 'replica' matches 'replicas', 'low-replica' and 'low replica count'. Verified: both replies the verify pass reported as failing now pass, as does the human span's own rendering ('many stateless workloads are designed to withstand ... low number of Pod replicas ... for stateful or batch workloads'). Lazy wrong replies fail: 'Stateful workloads and batch jobs suffer.' scores 2/4, 'All workloads are affected by pod recreation.' scores 0, and a stem echo scores 0. Residual, stated plainly: the matcher is a bag of words, so a reply that names all four categories with the roles reversed would pass. That is unfixable within this matcher and was equally true of the old key; the alternative is a long key that fails correct answers, which is the defect being repaired.

repairs.after: {"q": "Which changes does the proposal rule out as non-goals?", "answer": "Changing a pod's QoS class, resizing non-restartable init containers, evicting lower priority pods to make room, resource types other than CPU and memory, CPU or memory manager policies other than the default None, and resolving scheduler race conditions", "accept": ["qos class, init containers, evicting lower priority pods, scheduler races", "init containers, lower priority pods, scheduler races", "changing qos class, non restartable init containers, eviction of lower priority pods, resource types beyond cpu and memory, non default cpu and memory manager policies, and scheduler race conditions"]}
repairs.rationale: The first repair retargeted q3 at runtime_spec_depth, which exists only in the facts array and the human span. I re-ran the verify pass's grep against the rfc-01 prompt and confirm it: the prompt says only that the expected runtime behaviour 'is not documented'; 'high-level', 'implementation specifics' and 'non-goal to define' are all absent. Candidates never see the facts array, so A/B/C/D scored zero by construction and H scored one. The item measured the condition, not the writing. I retargeted rather than adding the fact to the brief prompt, because rewriting a brief changes what every condition writes and invalidates any output already produced against it. The new target is scope_limits, which is verbatim in the brief prompt ('Non-goals: QoS class change, non-restartable init containers, evicting lower-priority pods to make room, resource types other than CPU and memory, CPU/memory manager policies other than None, and resolving scheduler races') and inside the human span, whose 508 words run from kep-1287 line 163 to line 230 and therefore contain the whole Non-Goals section. It is an enumeration, so it is not cold-recoverable, and it shares no vocabulary with q1 (who is hurt), q2 (three triggers), q4 (CRI read-back) or q5 (who decides after a failed resize). It also restores coverage the first pass dropped: the old q4 graded the 'None' manager policy, which is one item of this list. Keys are built so that no two-item answer passes: accept[1] is a seven-token key needing six, so a reply naming only QoS class and scheduler races scores 2/7. Verified three correct renderings pass, including one that spells 'eviction' and 'race conditions' rather than 'evicting' and 'races'; 'It is a non-goal to control the full lifecycle of a pod whose resize failed.' fails, so the item does not collide with q5.

unrepaired.why: Left ungraded rather than injected into the brief prompt. It is a real fact of the source and it sits in the human span, but adding it to the prompt is a brief rewrite, which changes the writing task for every condition and would need the lift and word-band measurements redone. Nothing else in rfc-01 grades it, and nothing needs to: the five items now cover who_is_hurt, why_resources_change, scope_limits, cri_gap_readback and secondary_goals.
